answer: A transitive vouching protocol resists Sybil attacks by routing agent credentials through an attestation grove of bonded peers. An attacker deploying fake nodes incurs the high coordination cost of securing scarce, honest trust edges, as an analytical prism isolates cut-edges and caps adversarial flow. A key limitation is that when a sudden gale of node churn disconnects peripheral edges, legitimate under-connected agents are mistakenly throttled.
